\section{Groups}
A group\index{group} is a set with an associative operation.
\index{group!abelian}An abelian group is one whose operation commutes.
\index{ring|(}A ring has two operations.
\newpage
\section{Rings}
A field\index{field} is a ring whose nonzero elements form a group\index{group}.
\index{ring|)}\index{module|see{ring}}
The space\index{$L^2$ space} of square-integrable functions, by the
theorem\index{Theorem, 2nd form}\index{group!cyclic, of order 2}.
A set\index{set} is not a group\index{set} until it has
an operation\index{set}.
A group is finite when its order\index{order} is, that is\index{finite}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:order}|G| < \infty,\end{equation}
as in (\ref{eq:order}).
